candidates.name: eventstudy (LemaireJean-Baptiste)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package (69 stars, last updated Dec 2023) for financial event-study computation: single-event and multiple-event abnormal-return and CAR calculations against a market-model benchmark, significance testing. No bundled dataset -- takes user-supplied returns. Also on PyPI as `eventstudy`.
candidates.why_useful: Directly usable to run a rigorous event study around the 5 Nov 2026 ABNB print (and past 23 prints) for CAR/abnormal-return significance testing -- addresses gap #17 (event-study packages).
candidates.license: unspecified in README excerpt (check LICENSE file)

candidates.name: eventstudies (NIPFP)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (485 commits, CRAN v1.2.2, GPL-2) for event-study methodology from India's National Institute of Public Finance and Policy. Ships sample datasets (SplitDates, StockPriceReturns, OtherReturns) plus an `eventstudy()` function supporting market-model adjustment, custom event windows, cumulative-sum remapping, and bootstrap inference.
candidates.why_useful: A mature, peer-reviewed-adjacent event-study toolkit with bootstrap inference (more rigorous than naive t-tests) -- usable for ABNB earnings-day and regulatory-event studies (gap #12 regulatory events, #17 methods).

candidates.name: pandas-datareader
candidates.what_it_holds: Widely-used Python library (934+ commits) with a built-in FamaFrenchReader that pulls Ken French factor portfolios (3-factor, 5-factor, momentum, industry portfolios) directly from Dartmouth's data library in one line (`pdr.famafrench.FamaFrenchReader(...).read()`), plus FRED, World Bank, OECD, Eurostat, Bank of Canada readers.
candidates.why_useful: One-command, always-current pull of Ken French factors for building ABNB factor loadings / risk-adjusted event-study returns -- exactly what 'Ken French factor loaders' in the theme asks for, and we already hold static Ken French factors per CONTEXT.md, so this is the live-refresh method for keeping that series current.
candidates.time_coverage: full Ken French library history via live pull
candidates.size_hint: library only; data pulled on demand
candidates.last_activity: active (16 open PRs at check time)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold Ken French factors (static); this is a maintained pull method, not a new file.

candidates.name: earnings-vol-study
candidates.what_it_holds: Python event study of 639 earnings announcements across 54 large-cap US stocks, 2023-2026, built on free DoltHub options/price data. Committed CSVs in /data/: universe.csv (54 tickers), events.csv (earnings dates), event_panel.csv (full implied-vol/price/straddle panel, ~500-639 rows), events_enriched.csv, plus JSON result files (rq1/rq2/rq3, multiple-testing correction). Findings: IV rises ~7.6 vol pts pre-announcement and crushes ~7.3 pts post; implied move (~4.6% median) exceeds realized move (~3.7%), premium ratio 1.22x (p=0.041); pre-event IV is dominant crush-magnitude driver (R2=0.50). Includes data-quality audits, out-of-sample splits, placebo tests, unit tests.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme: a recent (through 2026), reproducible earnings-implied-move / IV-crush dataset and methodology built entirely on free data (DoltHub). If ABNB is among the 54 tickers this gives a ready calibration for the 5 Nov 2026 options-implied move; even if not, the method + DoltHub data source is directly replicable for ABNB. Also flags DoltHub as a free options-data source worth checking separately (fills gap #17 earnings-implied-move estimators, complements the existing reverse-DCF market-implied-move work).
candidates.size_hint: ~600-row event panel + several supporting CSVs/JSON, 12 commits
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Complements, does not duplicate, our existing Bloomberg options workbook and reverse-DCF market-implied model (those are ABNB-specific and licensed/pull-date-anchored; this is free, cross-sectional, and gives an independent method).

candidates.name: Earnings-Implied-Move-Mispricing
candidates.what_it_holds: Research framework studying earnings-implied-move mispricing via option straddle prices vs. realized post-earnings moves. Notebooks build base/loose/strict event datasets of 9,804 / 9,022 / 7,412 earnings events (2018-2024) using WRDS, OptionMetrics, and CRSP; regresses straddle 'edge' (realized minus implied move) on pre-earnings IV, bid-ask spreads, open interest, volume, price; expanding-window OOS validation 2018-2020 train / 2021-2024 test; includes a research paper PDF.
candidates.why_useful: Large-sample (thousands of events) earnings-implied-move methodology directly applicable to ABNB's 5 Nov print, but the underlying data (WRDS/OptionMetrics/CRSP) is licensed and not redistributable -- only the method/code is freely usable, not the dataset itself.
candidates.size_hint: 7,412-9,804 event dataset (not redistributable; built from licensed WRDS/OptionMetrics/CRSP)
candidates.last_activity: unspecified (2 commits, likely a course/thesis project)

candidates.name: easy-event-study
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python package (3 stars, last updated Oct 2025) billed as 'Financial Event Study made easy' -- a lighter-weight alternative to the LemaireJean-Baptiste eventstudy package for computing abnormal/cumulative-abnormal returns.
candidates.why_useful: Actively maintained (2025) alternative event-study implementation; worth a fallback if the older eventstudy package proves unmaintained/incompatible with current pandas.

candidates.name: Post-Earnings-Announcement-Drift (investor attention)
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter-notebook replication package (11 commits) of the PEAD anomaly using a standard event-study/CAR framework over an event window t=0 to t=21. Adds Google Trends search volume as an investor-attention proxy (following Da, Engelberg & Gao 2011) and an 'earnings announcement congestion' measure (competing same-day earnings releases) to test delayed information incorporation. Reports an annualized Sharpe of ~1.76 for a resulting long-short strategy. Contains cached datasets, figures, and tables in output folders (exact tickers/row counts not stated in README).
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made PEAD + investor-attention replication combining exactly the two themes in scope (event-study drift, and a Google-Trends-as-attention-proxy method) -- useful as a template even though our team's own Google Trends test failed as a demand nowcast; this is a different application (attention/congestion, not level).
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified (uses Google Trends, so likely post-2011)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Google Trends already tested and found not to work as a demand nowcast; this is a distinct use (investor attention around earnings dates), not a re-flag of the same failed construction.

candidates.name: alphalens
candidates.what_it_holds: Quantopian's Python library for performance analysis of predictive (alpha) factors -- factor return/IC analysis, quantile spread returns, turnover. Archived (Quantopian shut down) but widely mirrored/forked; the maintained continuation is stefan-jansen/alphalens-reloaded.
candidates.why_useful: General factor-analysis tooling that could be applied to any ABNB-related signal (e.g., nights-nowcast residuals, ADR card) to test for factor-style predictive decay/IC the way a systematic desk would, complementing the harness's backtest scoring.
candidates.last_activity: archived (unmaintained); use stefan-jansen/alphalens-reloaded for current fork

candidates.name: alphalens-reloaded
candidates.what_it_holds: Actively maintained fork/continuation of Quantopian's alphalens for predictive-factor performance analysis (IC, quantile returns, turnover), compatible with current pandas.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as alphalens above but maintained -- preferred choice if the team ever wants formal factor-IC analysis on any ABNB signal.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same functional role as quantopian/alphalens above.
